_doc: Guard Conformance Registry (superscar #3 — over/under-match). Maps EVERY live textual guard to its GUILT proof (the guard fires on the historical bad case) and INNOCENCE proof (the guard does NOT fire on the adjacent legitimate case). Enforced by infra/guard-conformance/check_guard_conformance.py: a censused guard missing from here, a phantom test reference, or a test no CI workflow runs = FAIL. The mandate rule this executes: 'nessuna guardia mergiata senza un test di innocenza E di colpevolezza' (cicatrix-superscar.md #3). To add a guard: write both tests first, then register it here.

.claude/hooks/codex-spalla-trigger.sh.note: PostToolUse hook logging tool_input.command verbatim to ~/logs/codex-spalla-trigger.jsonl -- secret-bearing by construction (a Bash call can carry a credential in argv). Found world-readable (0644) and never redacted. MAGNITUDE stated as the conclusion that survives re-measurement, not as a count: 3 runs carry secret material -- 1 whole token (ends at char 151 inside the 200-char logged field) plus 2 truncation-clipped partials (both ending EXACTLY at char 200, the truncation boundary itself). The raw line counts are NOT stable and are no longer quoted as facts: this hook logs the greps that measure it, so the literal matched 14 lines at 2026-08-21T15:56Z and 24 at 2026-08-21T20:28Z (histogram 20x10/5x13/1x46/1x87/1x108) while the 3 secret-bearing runs did not move; earlier drafts of this note said '11 values, 108 chars each' (a LINE count as a VALUE count) and then '2 whole tokens' (a truncation artifact as two more complete secrets). FIX, two independent defenses: umask 077 plus an explicit chmod 0600 for pre-existing files ('>>' never changes an existing file's mode), and redaction of the secret VALUE before the 200-char truncation. MATCHER, after three failed attempts on this branch in alternating directions (none of them ever released on main): a bare-substring version ate ordinary commands; a delimited-SEGMENT version over-corrected and leaked TWELVE undelimited forms IN FULL (APIKEY= apikey= apiKey= AUTHTOKEN= SECRETKEY= accesskey= mytoken= TOKENS= pass= auth=, a JSON api_key body, a postgres://user:pw@db URL); a vocabulary-bounded version closed those and still leaked PGPASSWORD= 99 times in the live log because nobody lists 'PG'. SHIPPED design splits by WORD: (a) ANY alphanumeric prefix + TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/PASSWD/CREDENTIAL with optional plural and optional _/- suffix chain; (b) KEY -- and only KEY -- restricted to a bounded 21-word prefix vocabulary or no prefix, because KEY is the one credential word that routinely ENDS an innocent identifier (monkey, pubkey, nkeys, topkey, dictkeys); (c) bare generic pass=/pwd=/auth=; plus an optional quote between name and separator (JSON), a URL-userinfo rule, and a bare Bearer rule. RULE INTERACTION, and ORDER ALONE WAS NOT THE FIX -- two Gear-3 gates on this branch, in opposite directions. (i) With rule 2 first, a credential-ish NAME whose UNQUOTED value began with the word Bearer had exactly that word replaced -- 'X-Auth: Bearer <v>' logged as 'X-Auth=<REDACTED> <v>' -- destroying the only marker rule 4 had and leaving the token in the clear, LESS safe than not matching at all; the control 'Authorization: Bearer <v>' was unaffected, which is why a green suite hid it. The reorder to 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2 fixed that. (ii) THE MIRROR, which the reorder itself created and the SECOND gate found: rule 4 eats an 8+ char [A-Za-z0-9._-] run after Bearer, and a credential NAME is exactly such a run, so 'Bearer refresh_token=<v>' logged as 'Bearer <REDACTED>=<v>' -- marker on the NAME, value in the clear, output reading as if redaction fired; rule 1 does it too when a token prefix starts a NAME (echo ghp_MYTOKENS=<v>). So the cure is STRUCTURAL, not positional: every marker-anchored rule now carries ASSIGN_TAIL, an optional [=:] plus a full quoted-or-bare VALUE, and 7 guilt cases pin the class (both quote styles included -- the bare [^\s"']* tail first proposed would have left the quoted forms leaking). Order 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2 is kept because rule 4 before rule 3 still leaks a URL password, and all five non-current permutations of 2/3/4 fail the suite -- which proves the suite CONSTRAINS the order, never that the order is safe: the mirror leak passed all five permutation mutants and shipped anyway, because no case in the corpus had its shape. A mutation score is a statement about the corpus, not about the world. The Authorization-anchored Bearer alternation was MEASURED DEAD by the same test that removed the two wildcards -- replayed over the whole live log, keeping only the bare alternation is byte-identical (0 differing lines), keeping only the header one is not (3) -- and deleted. Both wildcards an earlier comment called load-bearing were MEASURED DEAD and deleted: the left (?:[A-Za-z0-9]+[_-])* (0/44 output differences -- the negative lookbehind does that work and the replacement re-emits group(1) verbatim) and the leading (?:--?)? (0/174), the latter also being the only mutant nothing could kill. PROOF: 93 cases (76 guilt / 15 innocence / 2 mode), widened from 3/1/1. Guilt spans both GitHub PAT families, bare + suffixed + undelimited names, one case per vocabulary prefix and per wide word, plurals, bare generics, BOTH quote styles, a JSON body, a URL userinfo password, a secret STRADDLING the 200-char truncation boundary (which is what pins redact-before-truncate), and Bearer. Innocence added three cases for RULES 3 AND 4 on 2026-08-22, which until then had NONE -- no case in the corpus contained 'Bearer' or '://' at all, so every over-match and boundary mutant in those two rules was unkillable: the URL rule's userinfo user class (a query string ?to=ops:admin@example.test), the Bearer rule's \b (flagbearer) and its {8,} length floor (a 'Bearer v2' PR title). It also covers the 8 measured casualties of the substring version (monkey=patch, --keyfile=, jq '.key = 1', StrictHostKeyChecking=no, KEYSPACE=prod, --publicKeyPath=, sed s/keyword=old/keyword=new/, redis-cli KEYS '*') plus three NON-KEY keyword substrings (PasswordAuthentication=no, TOKENIZER=fast, -k 'secret_scanning') -- added because an earlier note claimed the corpus spanned TOKEN/KEY/SECRET substrings while every occurrence in it was 'key'. Mode covers BOTH defenses separately: a fresh log born 0600, and a PRE-EXISTING 0644 log repaired to 0600. MUTATION, SCOPED to an enumerated set rather than to 'every alternation' -- the previous universal wording was answered by the Gear-3 gate with five counterexamples: 63 mutants, 62 killed, 1 EQUIVALENT and excluded from the score (proven unkillable: its replacement re-emits group(1) verbatim, 0 distinguishing inputs over 883 adversarial strings, 200k fuzz cases and the whole live log), covering the 6 rules, 5 wide words, 21 vocabulary prefixes, 3 bare generics, 3 value alternations, 5 optional quantifiers, the lookbehind, both case flags, the colon separator, the Bearer word-boundary and length floor, the URL userinfo user AND password classes, the gh[pousr]_ class, the re-addition of the deleted Authorization alternation, 2 over-match wideners, all 5 non-current permutations of rules 2/3/4, redact-before-truncate and both mode defenses. Driver asserts sha256 CHANGED before running the suite and byte-identical after restore, and carries an atexit/SIGTERM restore guard -- an earlier run was killed mid-mutant by a tool timeout and left the hook mutated on disk. RESIDUAL RISK, both directions (cicatrix #3). UNDER-match, measured not guessed: <any-prefix>KEY= outside the vocabulary (PUBKEY=, M5KEY=, QKEY=, ORIGINALAPIKEY=, MACHINEHMACKEY=) leaks in full -- the deliberate price of keeping monkey=patch innocent, 40 distinct names / 136 occurrences on the live log that the substring version caught and this one does not, most of them that version's own over-match; credential words outside the six (--pin=, --otp=, --salt=, --cookie=); Authorization: with anything but Bearer (Basic <b64>, opaque token); a POSITIONAL secret with no name (mytool deploy s3cr3t, mysql -pS3cr3t, netrc-style password <v>) unless it carries a known prefix; an UNQUOTED value containing a space (first word only); the entry formerly titled 'a POSITIONAL secret with no name' RE-LABELLED 2026-08-22 because its title contradicted its own example -- the class is a secret NOT JOINED TO A CREDENTIAL-ISH NAME BY = OR :, which includes every --flag <value> form (gh auth login --token <v>, mytool --api-key <v>, mysql --password <v>, echo <v> | gh secret set FOO, and curl -u admin:<v> / --user admin:<v>, which carry a : but hang it off a USERNAME); and NEW 2026-08-22 the UNDER-MATCH half of the dot-lookbehind, described everywhere until now only as over-match protection -- a SINGLE-SEGMENT attribute assignment leaks in full (c.token = <v>, jq '.password = <v>') while multi-segment names are still caught (cfg.api_key), plus an INDEX between name and separator (SECRETS[0]=<v>, TOKEN[0]=<v>). OVER-match, with its full damage rather than value-only: a legitimately-named non-secret redacts just as hard (PWD=/tmp, FEATURE_FLAG_KEY=, redis-cli --pattern 'keys:*'), the replacement SWALLOWS the rest of an unquoted value so sed -i 's/key=old/key=new/' loses its second half, and it NORMALISES the separator to = so a header or JSON 'name: value' is logged as name=<REDACTED> and stops being a replayable command. Measured rate on the real log: 2291 lines / 0.686% of 333,832 at 2026-08-21T22:49:57Z, HIGHER than the 1875 / 0.562% of the substring version rejected for over-matching (and 1253 / 0.376% for the segment-only one). Accepted deliberately: over-redacting a non-secret beats under-redacting a real one. TWO SHAPES BELONGING TO RULES 3 AND 4 were undisclosed until 2026-08-22: the bare Bearer alternation eats the next >=8-char [A-Za-z0-9._-] run in ANY text with no name, assignment or separator, so a PR title or commit message containing the word 'bearer' is mangled -- and gh pr create is TRIGGER RULE 1 of this very hook, i.e. a line it exists to record (corpus at 2026-08-21T22:50:35Z / 333,833 lines: 8 lines match, 10 matches, 3 with no digit at all, one of them the measuring session's own probe string); and rule 3 redacts a PORT sitting in the userinfo PASSWORD position (curl 'https://example.com:8443@evil.test/'), though it cannot fire on a genuine host:port, which has no @ after it. Neither was fixed: narrowing Bearer to require a digit would trade a 3-occurrence over-match for an under-match on an all-lowercase token, and the all-digits carve-out for the port was rejected on a number -- 0 of 367 live URL-userinfo matches have an all-digit password, so it fixes nothing real and opens an under-match on any numeric credential. Scale on that rule: 354 of the 367 are one test-fixture DSN. NOTE ON THIS REGISTRATION: check_guard_conformance's is_armed() is substring-based, so it cannot detect deletion of the run: step that executes this test -- verified by simulation (step removed -> still reports armed). The step is genuine today; its removal would not be caught here.

BLOCKED_SUBCMD_RE.note: W85 stash over-match FIXED 2026-07-06 (negative lookahead: read-only `stash list|show` pass, bare/mutating stash still blocked) — test_w85_stash_readonly.py converted from tripwire-pin to plain guilt+innocence per the pin's own instructions

_is_remote_dispatch.note: W92 (2026-07-11): the SAME function, previously wired only into the git-verb channel (W83), is now ALSO consulted by _write_hits_main — a 5th over-match of this guard was the file-write channel having zero remote-dispatch awareness at all. Direct unit coverage of _is_remote_dispatch itself stays owned by test_w83_remote_dispatch.py; the NEW call site's outcome is proven by test_w92_remote_write_dispatch.py under the _write_hits_main entry below. SUPERSEDED as a whole-command decision (6th over-match, same day, PR-gate finding): both call sites now use the SEGMENT-SCOPED `_is_position_remote_dispatched` instead — see that symbol below.

_is_position_remote_dispatched.note: 6th over-match (2026-07-11, found at PR-2266 gate before merge, same session as W92): `_is_remote_dispatch` was a WHOLE-COMMAND exemption on both channels — `ssh pro hostname && git pull origin main` and `ssh mini hostname && cp /tmp/x scripts/f.py` both got wrongly exempted because SOME segment (the prelude) was remote, even though the mutating verb/write-target lived in a LATER, LOCAL segment. Fix: `_segments()` splits the noise-stripped command on `&& || ; |`; this function answers whether the segment CONTAINING a given character offset is itself remote-dispatched. Both `_git_verb_verdict` and `_write_hits_main` now check every match/target against its OWN segment via `all(...)`/per-target loop, not the whole command. Direct-mention coverage stays owned by test_segment_scoped_dispatch.py's module docstring + `_write_hits_main`'s per-target loop (which mentions it by name); guard_fuzz_harness.py's outcome-level proof lives under `_git_verb_verdict`/`_write_hits_main` below (it never calls this symbol directly, only through those).

_git_verb_verdict.note: Pure decision function extracted from main() during the 6th-over-match fix (2026-07-11) SPECIFICALLY so guard_fuzz_harness.py can call the REAL logic instead of re-implementing it. The harness's ORIGINAL run_corpus() had hand-copied the git-verb decision path inline — that copy used the pre-fix whole-command `_is_remote_dispatch` check and drifted from `main()` the same day it was written, producing 24 false mismatches against cases the real guard already handled correctly. A fuzz harness testing its own stale reimplementation instead of the guard is the exact failure this tool exists to prevent; extracting a single callable source-of-truth closes that structurally, not just for today's drift.

_write_hits_main.note: W92 fix 2026-07-11: an ssh/scp/rsync-dispatched write with a RELATIVE destination used to resolve against the LOCAL session cwd, producing a phantom write-target into the main checkout for a write that never touches this machine. Fixed by consulting _is_remote_dispatch upstream of target extraction (same reuse discipline as the git-verb channel). 6th over-match (SAME session, PR-gate finding): the exemption was whole-command — now `_extract_write_targets` returns `(path, offset)` and each target is segment-scoped individually via `_is_position_remote_dispatched`.

_effective_git_target.note: tilde/env blind-spot fixed 2026-07-06 (expanduser+expandvars at the single choke point; found by the W85 live guilt-probe — the resolver sits UPSTREAM of BLOCKED_SUBCMD_RE)

_only_ffonly_pull.note: ff-only pull exception (2026-07-06, Zero directive). W91 fixed same day: the first version did a bare substring check and a shell COMMENT mentioning --ff-only opened the exception for a bare pull (4th over-match of this guard) — now FFONLY_PULL_SEGMENT_RE anchors the flag to the pull segment. 15 guilt + 7 innocence + 4 probe cases.

_main_tree_tracked_clean.note: PENDING-ARMS 'Pro main self-align strutturalmente chiuso' iteration 5 (2026-07-11): a runtime_state_allowlist.json (machine-scoped, mirrors scripts/lint_home_fork.py machine_label() convention) exempts 3 Pro-only continuously-rewritten tracked files from gating the ff-only exception. W91 lesson applied to the allowlist ITSELF: guilt (any other tracked-dirty file, a rename touching an allowlisted name, wrong machine, missing allowlist file all still gate) + innocence (exactly the 3 declared paths, or a subset, still opens) both proven.

_resolve_under_worktrees.note: W105 (2026-07-26): resolved a removal target by TRUNCATING to the first segment under .worktrees/, so `.worktrees/<outer>/.worktrees/<inner>` resolved to <outer> and removing a clean nested worktree was refused in the dirty OUTER's name — family #3 deciding on path SHAPE, not on the ENTITY the path names. Fix: return the INNERMOST worktree `git worktree list --porcelain` actually knows that equals-or-contains the target; the legacy truncation stays as the fallback when git cannot enumerate (it is also what correctly pins `rm -rf <dirty-wt>/subdir` to <dirty-wt>, the W80 protection). Guilt: outer-by-own-path and `rm -rf <dirty-wt>/sub` still BLOCK. Innocence: the clean nested worktree, by both `git worktree remove` and `rm -rf`, is ALLOWED — both innocence cases fail against the pre-fix hook, verified before the fix landed. Contract narrowed by the same cure: it now returns None for `.worktrees` itself (it names no single worktree) — that target is NOT safe, it is handled by `_unarmed_dirty_removal_target` through the victim list instead. ROUND 2 (same cross-family refuter re-run on the round-1 fix: REFUTED, 7 findings, 4 blockers) — with the registry DEAD the legacy truncation named the OUTER worktree again, so a clean outer waved through `rm -rf <outer>/.worktrees/<inner>` with the inner dirty: the original W105 defect resurrected by a slow `git worktree list`. Now: registry first (authoritative), filesystem evidence (`_looks_like_worktree`) only when the registry is dead — gated that way on purpose, because while git can answer, a `.git` inside a subdirectory (a vendored clone) must not steal the verdict from <wt> and lose the W80 protection. A path git knows AS a worktree is returned as itself even when it is NAMED `.worktrees`. Corpus case red against the round-1 hook.

_worktrees_strictly_inside.note: The under-match twin W94 predicts for any over-match fix. `.worktrees/` is gitignored, so `git status` inside an OUTER worktree is blind to a worktree nested in it: removing the outer reads CLEAN while destroying the nested one's uncommitted work. The dirtiness probe cannot see these victims — only the worktree registry names them. Guilt: `rm -rf <clean-outer>` holding a DIRTY nested worktree BLOCKS (fails against the pre-fix hook). Innocence: clean-outer + clean-nested is still ALLOWED. Hardened after a cross-family adversarial round (Codex gpt-5.6-terra, verdict REFUTED, 11 findings): victims are scoped to the path being REMOVED, not to everything under the worktree that path belongs to (`rm -rf <clean-wt>/build-cache` was blocking on an unrelated dirty nested worktree — an over-match introduced by the over-match cure); an empty `_git_worktree_list()` means the probe DIED, not that nothing is nested, so it falls back to the filesystem, scoped to the `.worktrees` directory alone (walking the worktree itself would return ordinary subdirectories, and `git -C <subdir> status` answers for the enclosing worktree — a fresh over-match inside the fix); and the result is sorted so the victim a block message names is deterministic instead of inheriting `git worktree list` ordering. ROUND 2: the dead-registry filesystem fallback yielded ANY directory under `.worktrees/`, including ordinary ones that are not worktrees; it now filters on `_looks_like_worktree`, the same entity test the rest of the cure uses.

_unarmed_dirty_removal_target.note: Judges every VICTIM of the removal (the named target plus every registered worktree strictly inside it), not just the token the command spelled out. Previously judged the resolved target alone. (test_arm_keep_hook.py exercises this function end-to-end for the non-nested W80 cases but never names it, so it is deliberately NOT listed here — the anti-phantom rule wants a test that mentions the symbol, not one that merely happens to run through it.) ROUND 2: the container test was on the NAME alone, and `.worktrees` is a legal name for a worktree — such a worktree got judged by its children while its own uncommitted work burned. Now tested by ENTITY (registry, or `_looks_like_worktree` when the registry is dead). Corpus case red against the round-1 hook.

_token_to_worktrees_path.note: Token normalization split out of `_resolve_under_worktrees` during the W105 cure (2026-07-26), because the two callers need DIFFERENT answers for the same token. It keeps every conservative gate that predates it (drop shell-metacharacter residue; demand a literal `.worktrees` segment before resolving a relative token against a cwd that may itself sit inside a worktree — the W83 anti-auto-incrimination rule) and now also returns `.worktrees` ITSELF as a legitimate target. That last part closes a measured hole: `rm -rf <repo>/.worktrees` used to sail through, because the resolver returned None for a target it could not name as a single worktree, so the guard allowed wiping EVERY worktree including dirty unarmed ones (guilt case in the corpus, fails against the pre-fix hook). The root target is answered by its VICTIMS, never by its own `git status` — `git -C .worktrees status` reports the MAIN checkout's dirtiness, an unrelated verdict that would have been a fresh over-match. Same round: `rm -rf <...>/.worktrees/*` is normalized to the container it names (the metacharacter gate used to drop it as shell residue and let it wipe everything), and a token whose final component is a SYMLINK is refused — `rm -rf <link>` removes the link, not the referent, so resolving it first incriminated a worktree the command never touches. A trailing slash is the opposite intent (addressing the directory through the link) and stays in scope. ROUND 2: two more shapes reached past it. `rm -rf <root>/.worktrees/*/` — the same glob one keystroke different — fell to the metacharacter gate and wiped every worktree unseen; and `rm -rf <symlink>/*` deleted the referent's contents, because the round-1 code exempted a glob from the terminal-symlink refusal only by accident of ordering. Both cured by carrying the 'reaches THROUGH the target' fact explicitly (the `through` flag trailing-slash already used) and normalizing `/*/` as well as `/*`. DECLARED RESIDUE, not silently accepted: a directory literally named `*` is read as the container (a possible false BLOCK), because trusting the literal name would turn a glob removal of EVERY worktree into a verdict about one of them — an under-match on a destructive command. Both cases red against the round-1 hook.

_remote_discard_on_main.note: W117 (2026-08-10): a NEW channel, because the git-verb channel structurally cannot see this. `_strip_noise()` empties quoted text by design (W83, so `grep "git pull"` is not read as a command), so `ssh pro 'cd ~/nuzantara && git reset --hard origin/main'` reaches `_git_verb_verdict()` as no_blocked_verb — the remote-dispatch exemption is never even consulted. MEASURED before the cure was written: an earlier draft sat inside that exemption branch and would have been dead code on the only path it exists for (W116). The gap bit the same day: that command, run to realign Pro's main checkout, discarded 159 entries of the intel publish ledger (whose loss RE-PUBLISHES already-published articles) and 24 open escalations — runtime state no commit holds, named in `runtime_state_allowlist.json`, which is exactly why `scripts/pro/pro-git-pull.sh` backs those files up and restores them around the fast-forward. This channel re-reads the ssh payload on purpose (`_ssh_payloads`), then applies `_strip_noise` INSIDE it so a verb quoted within the payload stays innocent. Fail-closed when the payload names no path at all (a bare `ssh pro 'git reset --hard'` runs in an unknowable remote cwd, and these verbs are the ones git cannot undo). Innocence: `ssh pro git pull` still exempt, a remote `.worktrees/` path allowed (a worktree carries no runtime state), W85 read-only `stash list|show` spared, and a LOCAL reset after a remote probe is left to the git-verb channel rather than misattributed here. The `.worktrees` exemption lives in `_names_main_checkout` and NOWHERE else: a mutation survived against a second copy of it, and the survivor was not a missing test but a REDUNDANT guard that was ALSO an under-match — `cd <worktree> && git -C ~/nuzantara reset --hard` names both, and the short-circuit waved the main-checkout reset through. `_names_main_checkout` judges by path COMPONENT, not basename: `~/nuzantara/apps` is inside the checkout and the reset discards the whole worktree there too. Corpus 13 guilt + 11 innocence, mutation-verified 8/8.

_looks_like_worktree.note: The ENTITY test the W105 round-2 cure is built on (2026-07-26): a linked worktree root carries a `.git` FILE, an ordinary directory sitting under `.worktrees/` does not. Used in exactly two places and no more — as the dirtiness probe's precondition, and as filesystem evidence when the worktree registry is unavailable. Deliberately NOT used while `git worktree list` can answer: a `.git` inside a subdirectory (a vendored clone) would otherwise steal the verdict from the worktree that actually owns the path and drop the W80 protection.

_worktree_is_dirty.note:
W105 round 2 (2026-07-26): the probe answered for the WRONG checkout. `git -C

status` reports the state of whatever ENCLOSES

, so an ordinary directory under `.worktrees/` (a pruned worktree's husk, a scratch dir) was judged by the MAIN checkout's dirtiness — never empty, i.e. a permanent false BLOCK on removing something that holds nothing to lose. Not a regression of the round-1 fix: the shape predates W105 and was only found because the refuter attacked the function NEXT TO the cured one. It now refuses to answer for a path that is not a worktree root, which gives up nothing — `.worktrees/` is gitignored, so no tracked file of the enclosing checkout can live under such a directory. Innocence: the ordinary-directory removal is ALLOWED (red against the round-1 hook). Guilt: every dirty-worktree case in the corpus still BLOCKS. Fail-open on a probe error is deliberate and unchanged — blocking on a git hiccup is what teaches people to disarm the guard.

infra/claude-hooks/guard_fuzz_harness.py.note: Reusable property/fuzz corpus runner for worktree_isolation.py's two decision channels (git_verb + write_target) — 445 generated command shapes (quotes, comments, newlines, heredocs, pipes, ssh-wrapping, git-verbs-inside-strings, true-compound remote-prelude-plus-local-mutation) classified against a fixture, not a hand-picked example list. Self-executing: `python3 infra/claude-hooks/guard_fuzz_harness.py` exits 1 on any unexplained mismatch. Guard-agnostic design (Case/run_corpus) intended for reuse by a future guard's own corpus generator. STRUCTURAL FIX (2026-07-11, 6th over-match): run_corpus's git_verb branch now calls `mod._git_verb_verdict()` directly instead of re-implementing the decision inline — the inline copy had drifted from the real guard the same day it was written (see _git_verb_verdict's registry note).

infra/claude-hooks/host_boundary.py.note: The carve-out half (UNPROTECTED_SUBPATHS) lived only in the live ~/.claude copy from 2026-06-16 until it was promoted on 2026-08-12; test_host_boundary.py never named it, so it passed with or without. test_host_boundary_carveout.py pins both directions — the freed subpaths stay writable, the control plane stays shut — and is mutation-verified: emptying UNPROTECTED_SUBPATHS kills exactly the three cases that carry weight (memory, scripts, venvs).

infra/claude-hooks/orchestrate_gate.py.note: Was censused with tests:[] and excused by also_covered_by:vaccine. Measured 2026-08-12 against live M5 transcripts: 4 of its 5 dispatch keywords named Task/TaskCreate and scored ZERO occurrences ever, and the 5th (subagent_type) is an OPTIONAL parameter — so the guard was blind to the live Agent tool and would have kept blocking a caller who had just dispatched. Now matches Agent/Task/TaskCreate by tool name (JSON-spacing tolerant) plus isSidechain, and refuses to convict on a transcript whose shape it cannot recognize (W106b: cannot-verify is not a verdict). Corpus is mutation-verified — restoring the dead vocabulary kills 4 tests. Second, independent defect found the same day (lesson_a_disarmed_gate_is_mute_2026_08_12): the kill switch itself (ORCHESTRATE_GATE_OFF=1) produced zero signal when set — it was inherited from a launching shell, written in no file, and a 6400-line/0-dispatch session was never blocked without a trace anywhere. The disarmed path now emits one notice per session (systemMessage + hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, the latter verified to reach Claude's own context per the current hooks doc) stating the real transcript-line-count/dispatch-count and whether the gate WOULD have blocked — never blocking itself. Mutation-verified: 4 independent targeted mutants (notice fully disabled, would-block claim inverted, once-per-session dedup removed, cannot-verify guard removed) each kill exactly the test(s) that check that property and nothing else; a 5th mutant on the armed-path wording confirms the pre-existing block behaviour stays byte-identical while disarmed.

infra/claude-hooks/data_plane_guard.py.note: registry-based PreToolUse guard (2026-07-16): blocks interactive hand-edits of curated datasets outside their program's sanctioned compiler scripts (infra/claude-hooks/data-plane-registry.json). 14 guilt+innocence cases against a synthetic git tree prove worktree-aware path relativization (the .git-walk-up, not a hardcoded main-checkout root), missing-registry pass-through, and the kill switch.

exempt.infra/claude-hooks/dispatch_nudge.py: advisory transcript reminder (CLAUDE.md §7 T1.1) — emits a nudge, never blocks a command; no block/allow contract to test
exempt.infra/claude-hooks/prove_live_installed_: not a hook: it PROVES one. Feeds the real PreToolUse payload to the INSTALLED ~/.claude/hooks/worktree_isolation.py and reads its verdict — the gap CI structurally cannot cover, since every suite here judges the repo copy while the deciding file is a real copy under $HOME (W81: merged != armed). It carries its own 17-case guilt+innocence corpus and its own two cannot-verify exits (kill-switch set, hook absent), and it must NEVER be added to a CI step: ~/.claude/hooks does not exist on a runner, so it would exit 2 there by construction.

detect_secrets_content_keyed_rules._doc: CONTENT_KEYED_RULES in scripts/detect_secrets_auto_triage.py — path-scoped AND content-keyed (assignment-target name) auto-triage rules, added so a detect-secrets false-positive fix can't degrade into a blanket whole-file path rule (superscar #3). PR #3127 registered the first entry: worker-plane review panel executable identity pins (sha256/cdhash). 2026-07-26 added a second entry: apps/mouth/data/kbli-gold-all.json's sentence_sha256 idempotency marker — content-keyed rather than path-only because, unlike this repo's other KBLI auto-approve rules, that file has an open (not data-plane-guarded) writer set. 2026-07-28 added a third: the source_sha256 freshness stamp in translated articles (apps/mouth/src/content/articles/**/*.<locale>.mdx), written by scripts/translate-articles.py so the hourly translator can skip on freshness instead of on the target file's existence — 1294 of them, flagged as Hex High Entropy Strings by shape, recomputable from the public English article and never credentials. Content-keyed for the same reason again, at the widest scale yet: article .mdx files are written by the translator, the editorial pipeline AND humans, so a path rule would blanket-approve any future finding across 2500+ content files.

codex_seat_census.note: Census guard (2026-08-12): every file in the tree that invokes `codex exec` must resolve a seat through scripts/lib/codex_seat.sh|.py, so a NEW call site fails here instead of on Pro at 03:00 — W107, curing one wrapper of five only changes WHICH caller dies on a dead seat. Guilt+innocence for the detector itself in test_the_census_detector_tells_an_invocation_from_prose: guilt = argv and shell invocations in both quote styles are seen; innocence = a docstring merely naming the command, `mycodex exec` and `codex execute-plan` are not (the first draft matched prose, and an exemption list padded with false positives is a list nobody reads). Census verdict in test_no_call_site_invokes_codex_without_choosing_a_seat; every exemption carries a written reason. Why it exists: measured on all three machines by REPLY and not by exit code (W104) — Pro's default ~/.codex answers 401 while a paid, logged-in seat sat one env var away, and the second ChatGPT Pro subscription was touched by nothing anywhere. Armed per-PR by immune-enforcement.yml.
